newsitem.title: USA: Nursing hurt knee, Clinton taps "English Patient".
newsitem.headline: Nursing hurt knee, Clinton taps "English Patient".

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton, who is nursing an injured right knee, may support "The English Patient" at Monday night's Oscars ceremony because he feels "sympathies for patients," White House spokesman Mike McCurry joked.

Asked by reporters who Clinton was supporting at the 69th annual Academy Awards, McCurry initially said he did not know, then added: "Let's pick 'The English Patient' -- a sure winner. He's got sympathies for patients."

Clinton had surgery to repair a torn knee tendon 10 days ago and is using a wheelchair and crutches as he recovers. His doctors say he may be on crutches for eight weeks, adding it may take six months before he can resume jogging and golf.

"The English Patient," a story of a man dying from his injuries in the second World War and of his romance with a married British woman, has picked up 12 Oscar nominations, including one for Best Picture.
